name: openworker
label: OpenWorker
description: Local-first agent coworker driven headlessly through its own server

check_ready.not_ready_message: No model API key — pick a provider and set OPENWORKER_API_KEY (press e to configure)
check_ready.unreadable_message: The OpenWorker model key could not be read. Re-enter OPENWORKER_API_KEY in the Configure screen.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_PROVIDER
env_config.description: Which model provider the API key belongs to. OpenWorker is bring-your-own-model, so this decides both the endpoint and how the model id is routed. Use ollama for a local server, or openai-codex to reuse a ChatGPT subscription (which also needs OPENWORKER_STATE_DIR).

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_API_KEY
env_config.description: API key for the provider selected above. Passed to the OpenWorker server in its environment and never written to disk. Leave blank only for ollama, or when reusing a state directory that already holds credentials.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_BASE_URL
env_config.description: Endpoint override — for a relay, a self-hosted gateway, Azure OpenAI, or where `ollama serve` is listening. Leave blank to use the provider's official endpoint.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_MODEL
env_config.description: Model id to run on. Leave empty for the OpenWorker default; the provider prefix is added automatically, so plain `claude-opus-5` is enough when the provider is anthropic.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_MODE
env_config.description: Permission mode for each turn. `bypass-approvals` is the default because nobody is at the keyboard to approve tool calls; its hard floors (settings files, writes outside the workspace, .git/hooks) still apply. `interactive` and `auto-approve` will stall on anything that asks.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_ALLOW_TOOL_INSTALL
env_config.description: Set to 1 to let the agent install tools from OpenWorker's pinned catalog on its own. Off by default — a declined request is a supported outcome and the agent falls back and says so.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_STATE_DIR
env_config.description: Advanced. Where the OpenWorker server keeps its conversations and credentials. Blank means a private directory under ~/.openagents. Point it at the desktop app's state directory (~/.config/coworker, or %APPDATA%\coworker) to reuse its sign-ins — but only while that app is closed, since two processes must never write one store.

tagline: Everything stays on your machine: the agent loop, the conversations, the model keys. Installed with uv.
